title: The browser cache and its effect on tests

videos.script: A browser keeps copies of what it has been sent. That is why the second visit to a site is faster than the first. {{cache}} It is also why a customer can see a price that changed ten minutes ago. {{offer}} In this lesson the shop gets an offer page with a flaw. The server tells the browser to keep the offer for ten minutes. You change the offer, open the page again in the same browser, and the old price comes back. The server never hears the second request. {{log}} Then the surprise. Your tests do not see this at all. Playwright gives every test a new, empty browser context. That makes a test repeatable, and it also makes every test a first-time visitor. {{contexts}} So you write the returning customer on purpose. Two visits in one context. {{test}} You check the headers the server sends, since they are the promise the browser keeps. {{headers}} And you find out which of your own habits switch the cache off without telling you. {{route}}
